verdicts.evidence: Preflight.jl:212-214 now reads: '`anchor` is whether the hat runs at full strength... It is unrelated to the `file#heading` anchors of [`Config.resolve_anchor`](@ref).' Explicit disambiguation with @ref at the second sense's first use.

GBGCodingTools.jl module docstring (module #1, read before all others) now states: 'An instrument is one of four review procedures: check-docs, check-consistency, bug-hunt, audit-changes.' DocLints.jl:11 and Preflight.jl:313 also name the four and @ref back to GBGCodingTools.

GBGCodingTools.jl defines 'the gate' once with @ref. DocLints.jl:18 and TestHarness.jl:582 both say '[`GBGCodingTools.gate`](@ref), the generic closure gate' vs the consumer's own gate ('Never the bare four-instrument gate'). CLI/Gate.jl:71 labels cmd_gate 'the CLI face of [`gate`](@ref)'. All three cross-linked and named distinctly.

GBGCodingTools.jl (module #1): 'A lane is one agent's share of a round — one surface, one territory, or one kind of change.' Schema.jl:40-42 (module #5, first true use) repeats this and @ref-links GBGCodingTools; Scan.jl:39 restates it inline too.

GBGCodingTools.jl: 'A hat is one persona of the check-consistency panel, reading the corpus from a single standpoint' (module #1). Preflight.jl:199 (resolve_hats) restates this before the field list; Init.jl:233 now says '(`Preflight.resolve_hats` binds the term)'.
Reflection.jl:164 now reads: 'the [`GBGCodingTools.Ledger`](@ref)'s `[exemption.match]` predicate' — @ref-linked and qualified at first mention, per RULE.DOC.XLINK.

GBGCodingTools.jl: 'A Workflow is the instrument's `workflow/*.js` script, launched by the session running the round.' Schema.jl:41-42 restates and @ref-links back; Preflight.jl:9 module docstring also spells it out.
